notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 06/11/2025
Patient: Natalie Boehm, 82-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 06/11/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 40.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 4% of all events. The study demonstrated predominantly obstructive respiratory events leading to significant sleep fragmentation. Oxygen saturation levels showed intermittent desaturation episodes associated with apneas and hypopneas. Sleep stages were otherwise within normal limits. These results indicate severe sleep apnea requiring further clinical management.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/06/2026
Patient: Natalie Boehm, 83-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea with ongoing symptoms despite CPAP therapy.

History:
Ms. Boehm has a history of obstructive sleep apnea and has been using CPAP therapy consistently every night. She reports continued daytime fatigue and unrefreshing sleep.

Physical Examination:
BMI 24.2 kg/m2.
No significant abnormalities noted on general examination.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 21.8 events/hour on CPAP at 12 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates persistent moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea despite adherence to CPAP therapy at an adequate pressure setting.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including bilevel positive airway pressure or advanced modalities.
2. Referral to a sleep technologist for mask fit reassessment and possible pressure titration.
3. Follow-up sleep study to evaluate efficacy of any new interventions.
4. Continue monitoring symptoms and adherence.

Summary:
Ms. Boehm's obstructive sleep apnea remains inadequately controlled with current CPAP therapy, necessitating further evaluation and management adjustments.
